questions.q: Why do people so often choose urgent tasks over important ones?
a: Busyness feels like status, and checking tasks off gives a chemical rush
Important tasks are usually harder to identify in advance
Urgent tasks almost always produce better long-term results
Important tasks rarely require any planning or effort
questions.why: Lesson 1 names urgency as a status symbol and to-do lists as a dopamine hit.

questions.q: What is the purpose of imagining your 80th birthday?
a: It clarifies your vision, which makes today's decisions easier
It helps you calculate how much money you must save
It reveals which friends will still be around later
It sets a deadline for finishing your career goals
questions.why: Lesson 2 says a clear picture of the future keeps choices aligned with what matters.

questions.q: What does Covey say our mindset should shift away from?
a: Independence and competition toward interdependence and cooperation
Long-term planning toward quick daily wins
Family time toward professional ambition
Personal values toward external measures of success
questions.why: Lesson 3 says cooperation and win-win thinking produce better results.

questions.q: What should you do when an urgent request conflicts with a commitment you made?
a: Say no to the urgent request and keep the commitment
Cancel the commitment and accept the urgent request
Try to do both at once with divided attention
Let the other person decide which one matters more
questions.why: Lesson 1 says protecting commitments prevents distrust and later regret.

questions.q: What does the Apple example illustrate in lesson 3?
a: No single person can build a complex product alone
Great leaders must personally understand every detail
Competition between departments improves quality
Technology matters more than the people behind it
questions.why: Lesson 3 says even Steve Jobs depended on many specialists cooperating.
